identificationModule.briefTitle: Efficacy and Safety Study of R935788 Tablets to Treat Rheumatoid Arthritis
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase II, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel Dose Study of Two Doses of R935788 in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients Failing to Respond to Methotrexate

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether the Spleen Tyrosine Kinase (Syk) inhibitor, R935788 (R788), at a dose of 100 mg, orally, twice-a-day, and/or a dose of of 150 mg, orally, once-a-day is effective in the treatment of Rheumatoid Arthrits in patients who have had an inadequate clinical response to methotrexate.

armGroups.description: R788, 150 mg tablet, orally, once a day
Placebo, orally, either once a day, or twice a day

interventions.name: Fostamatinib disodium (R935788)
interventions.description: 150 mg tablet, orally, once a day

interventions.name: Placebo
interventions.description: Placebo, orally, either once a day, or twice a day

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Disease Activity Score-C-Reactive Protein (DAS28-CRP) <2.6 at 1 Month
secondaryOutcomes.description: Number of participants with DAS28-CRP (measuring RA symptoms including: tender joint count, swollen joint count, patient's assessment of disease activity, and CRP in patients with high CRP at baseline), of less than 2.6. The DAS runs from 0 to 10 - higher scores indicate worse symptoms. A score of less than 2.6 indicates remission of RA symptoms

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue (FACIT-F) at 6 Months
secondaryOutcomes.description: Change from baseline in FACIT-F, which is a patient-reported 13-item questionnaire that assesses fatigue, calculated as the score at 6 months minus the score at baseline. The FACIT-F runs from 0 to 52 with lower scores indicating higher fatigue. A positive change from baseline indicates an improvement in fatigue after treatment.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) Physical Component Summary (PCS) at 6 Months
secondaryOutcomes.description: Change from baseline in the PCS of the SF-36 (which assesses health and wellbeing), calculated as the score at 6 months minus the score at baseline. The PCS ranges from 0 to 100 with 100 indicating the highest level of functioning possible. A positive change indicates an improvement in PCS after treatment
